lanes.notes: Recent median 92s, observed max 248s. PMD does not run here, and the record of why is the point of this note: tempdoc 930 §22.2 follow-up 10 briefly put the `Static analysis (PMD, all source sets)` step in this lane (matrix `if`) on the expectation that a lane already compiling test sources would run `pmdAll` cheaper than `Build (no model blobs)`, where it measured 188s. Measured, the expectation was wrong — 201s here, and the lane at 487-488s (259s tests + 201s PMD) OVER its 360s advisory budget, while the origin job runs 469s against 600s. `pmdAll` needs main AND every non-main source set for all ~30 modules, whereas this lane compiles `test` for only fifteen and `assemble` had already compiled all of main. The step went back to `Build (no model blobs)`. Do not relocate it here again without re-measuring — that is the move this note exists to stop.

Follow-up 2 of tempdoc 930 §22.2 added a pmdMain step on top of the completed assemble (49s of a 352s job, run 33958691983); follow-up 10 widened it to `pmdAll` over every Java source set, measured at 188s here (run 33967299967, job 469s against this 600s budget). PMD's own analysis is only ~22s for all 72 tasks once classes exist, so the rest is compiling test sources, which `assemble` does not do. That step was then tried in `Unit tests (platform-contracts)` on the theory that a lane already compiling tests would run it cheaper: it did NOT — 201s there, that lane at 488s against its 360s budget, and this job down to 214-261s (runs 33967790388 and the head after it). `pmdAll` needs main plus every non-main source set for all ~30 modules, so neither placement avoids the compile and this is the job with the headroom; the step lives here. Do not relocate it again without re-measuring — relocating on an untested expectation is what produced that detour. The advisory budget is unchanged; re-read it against the next observed median.
